title: Florida's 45-Hour Post-Licensing Course: What New Agents Need to Know
metaDesc: Florida's 45-hour post-licensing course explained: when it's due, what happens if you skip it, the final exam format, and who qualifies for an exemption.

about: Florida's 45-hour post-licensing education requirement for new real estate sales associates

hub.name: Become a Real Estate Agent in Florida

answer: The Florida 45-hour post-licensing course is required education every new sales associate must complete before their first license renewal, which falls 18 to 24 months after the license is issued. It’s separate from your original pre-license course and separate from the 14-hour continuing education you’ll take every renewal after that. Skip it, and your license becomes null and void, meaning you’d have to start over as a brand-new applicant.
takeaways: The 45-hour post-licensing course is required once, before your very first Florida license renewal (18 to 24 months after you get licensed).
It's completely separate from the 14-hour continuing education (CE) you'll take at every renewal after that.
Miss the deadline and your license goes null and void, you'd have to re-qualify and re-apply as if starting over.
The course ends with a proctored, 3-hour, 100-question exam, and you need a 75% to pass.
Agents with a 4-year real estate degree may qualify for an exemption from the requirement.
tldr: New Florida sales associates must complete a 45-hour post-licensing course before their first renewal, 18 to 24 months after licensing, or the license becomes null and void. It's separate from the ongoing 14-hour CE requirement, ends in a 3-hour, 100-question exam (75% to pass), and a 4-year real estate degree can exempt you.
body:
What is the 45-hour post-licensing course?

When you pass your Florida sales associate exam and get licensed, that’s only the beginning of your required education. Florida requires every new sales associate to complete 45 hours of post-licensing coursework before their license’s first renewal. Think of it as a second round of training that builds on the basics from your pre-license course, this time with more practical, transaction-level detail now that you’re actually working with buyers and sellers.

When is it due?

Florida sales associate licenses are issued on a renewal cycle, and your first renewal comes 18 to 24 months after your license is issued, depending on when in the cycle you got licensed. The 45-hour course has to be finished before that first renewal date. It’s easy to assume you have years to get to it since real estate keeps you busy, but the clock is shorter than most new agents expect, so it’s worth scheduling early rather than waiting until the deadline is close.

How is this different from continuing education (CE)?

New agents often confuse the 45-hour course with ongoing CE, but they are two distinct requirements. The 45-hour post-licensing course is a one-time requirement tied only to your first renewal. After that, every subsequent renewal (typically every two years) requires 14 hours of continuing education instead, covering topics like core law and ethics updates. Post-licensing is the bridge between being brand new and being an established, renewing licensee; CE is what keeps you current for the rest of your career.

What happens if you don't complete it in time?

This is the part that catches people off guard: if you don’t finish the 45 hours before your first renewal, your license doesn’t just lapse or go inactive, it becomes null and void. That means the license itself ceases to exist. To practice again, you’d generally need to re-qualify from scratch, including retaking the required pre-license education and the state exam. Given how much time and money go into becoming licensed in the first place, missing this deadline is one of the most avoidable, and costly, mistakes a new agent can make.

What does the course cover, and how does it end?

The 45-hour curriculum digs into the real-world side of the business: real estate contracts, disclosures, closing procedures, escrow, agency relationships, and Florida-specific practice issues that a brand-new agent runs into on actual deals. It’s designed to fill the gap between passing a licensing exam and confidently handling a live transaction. The course concludes with a proctored final exam: 3 hours long, 100 questions, and a 75% score required to pass. If you don’t pass on the first attempt, most providers allow a retake, though policies vary by school.

Is there any way to be exempt?

Yes, in certain cases. Agents who hold a 4-year degree in real estate from an accredited institution may qualify for an exemption from the 45-hour post-licensing requirement. If this applies to you, don’t assume it happens automatically. You’ll need to confirm eligibility and file the appropriate paperwork with the state, so it’s worth checking your specific situation before assuming you’re covered.

How should a new agent plan around this?

The smartest approach is to treat the 45-hour course as part of your onboarding, not an afterthought to squeeze in later. Many new agents knock it out through an approved provider in the first several months while transaction details are still fresh, rather than racing the clock right before their renewal window closes. Building it into your first year, alongside your early deals and mentorship, means one less deadline hanging over you while you’re still learning the ropes.

What format does the course come in?

Approved providers generally offer the 45 hours in a few formats: in-person classroom sessions, live online classes, or self-paced online modules you work through on your own schedule. Which format fits best usually comes down to how you learn and how your first months of selling are shaping up. A brand-new agent juggling early showings and open houses might prefer a self-paced option they can chip away at in the evenings, while someone who learns better with a live instructor and classmates might choose an in-person or live virtual section instead. Either way, the 45 hours and the final exam requirement are the same regardless of format.

faq.q: How many hours is Florida's post-licensing course for new sales associates?
faq.a: 45 hours. It's required once, before your first license renewal, and is separate from the pre-license course you took to get licensed and the 14-hour CE you'll complete at later renewals.

faq.q: What happens if I don't finish the 45-hour course before my first renewal?
faq.a: Your Florida real estate license becomes null and void. You would generally need to re-qualify as a new applicant, including pre-license education and the state exam, so it's important not to let the deadline pass.

faq.q: What's on the final exam for the 45-hour post-licensing course?
faq.a: A proctored exam: 3 hours long with 100 questions, requiring a 75% score to pass. Retake policies for those who don't pass on the first try vary by course provider.

faq.q: Can I skip the 45-hour post-licensing course?
faq.a: Possibly, if you hold a 4-year real estate degree from an accredited institution, which may qualify you for an exemption. Confirm your eligibility and required paperwork with the state rather than assuming it applies automatically.
